new_token.description: If False (default), reuse your most recent active honeytoken instead of generating a new one; the name is only used when no reusable token exists and one must be created. tools.description: Open a GitGuardian incident from a pasted link or a bare incident ID. Start here when the user gives an incident link, or an incident ID without saying whether it is internal or public. A dashboard or public API incident link is read as the internal or Public Monitoring incident it points to. A bare ID is looked up as both, and the result says which matched, or that the ID is ambiguous. Returns the incident with its kind, ID and dashboard link. A link to an incidents list points to the list tools. Links for other instances or workspaces are refused; query strings and fragments are ignored; share-token links are unsupported.

incident_id.description: An incident ID given without saying whether it is internal or public. Both kinds are looked up, and the result says which one matched.

url.description: GitGuardian dashboard incident link (internal or public) or public API incident URL for this server's instance.

with_occurrences.description: Number of occurrences to include for internal incidents (0-100). Unused for public incidents.

tools.name: get_gitguardian_resource

outputSchema.description: The incident, which kind it is, and the identifiers it was found by.

url.description: The link without its query string and fragment, or, for a bare ID, the incident's dashboard link when the API returns one.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID from a dashboard link; null for API URLs and bare IDs.

tools.title: Resolve Public Incident

tools.description: Ask a secret's provider to revoke it, so that it can no longer be used: an incident's secret_id, internal or public. This cannot be undone, and everything that uses the secret stops working: confirm with the user first. It uses the workspace's default revocation credentials; only secrets whose detector has a revoker can be revoked, and success is false with a reason otherwise. The workspace must allow reading secrets through the API, which on GitGuardian SaaS also needs an IP allowlist; otherwise the API refuses with a 403.

secret_id.description: ID of the secret: an incident's secret_id, not its incident ID

tools.name: revoke_secret

outputSchema.description: What the provider did with the revocation request.

is_async.description: When success is true, whether the provider is still processing the revocation

reason.description: Why the request was not made, when success is false: no revoker for this detector, GitGuardian does not hold the value, a request was already made in the last hour, or the provider refused

success.description: Whether the revocation request was made to the provider

documents.description: The files to scan. Send only files that are part of the codebase and not ignored by .gitignore.
